body._note: canonical M1b body: every muscle group from spec/v2_muscles.js MUSCLE_GROUPS (no overrides)

ctrl._variant: B3 — BALANCE-3 candidate: C3 (A-mode = its COM objective, unchanged) + the H-mode (trunk-against-legs) eigenmovement objective on the mean hip angle, Alexandrov 2005 H-mode gains, with a COM-neutral ankle companion identified on this body

_provenance.delays: steps @240 Hz, rounded UP (never faster than human); literature §19.2: com 24 = task-level body/COM state → ankle (and knee) muscles 100 ms [D on MODEL]; comHip 18 = task-level body state → hip / trunk muscles 75 ms [D on M/MODEL]; orient 18 = the same, for the upper-body orientation offsets (position + integral); orientRate 8 = proprioceptive trunk / hip angular velocity 30 ms [MODEL] (Goodworth & Peterka 2009 25 ± 6 ms; outside W0); head 6 = vestibulocollic 22 ms [M]; leg 24 = task-level → leg muscles 100 ms (knee length, support symmetry); prop 24 = posture (weak, axes without task), conservative 100 ms [D]
_provenance.com: G: measured gravitational stiffness of the AP / ML COM mode on this body (design analysis, N/m) [E]; kP 1.33 / kD 0.45 s / kI 0.17 s⁻¹: Peterka 2002 / Pasma 2017 normalised gains [M/MODEL]; kA 0 (D2: a raw COM-acceleration difference is not a defensible sensor); eff [1, 1]: NO effectiveness compensation (D9: the fitted 0.65 ML compensation destabilised A at the literature delays); hipChannel: the hip axes of the COM map receive the COM state at the hip/trunk latency
_provenance.groups: hat (hips, sagittal) / trunk (lumbar) / upper (thoracic) / head (neck): gravity-load maps × kP 1.3, kD 0.45 s, kI 0.17 s⁻¹ (Peterka-type, D6) on the composite COM offset; offset on orient (75 ms), rate on orientRate (30 ms); head on the vestibulocollic channel
_provenance.knee: per-leg support length (D4); G 57.3 N·m/rad = measured squat-mode gravitational stiffness per knee [E]; kP 1.3 / kD 0.45 as the other gravity-load objectives (D5)
_provenance.support: D11 support symmetry: differential sagittal ankle objective; K_d per ankle DERIVED from entry geometry (b1_ctrl.mjs) [E]; kP 1.3, kI 0.17 as the other gravity-load objectives; kD 0 because the measured open-loop differential mode is viscous (no inertial oscillation; high-frequency loop gain kD·K_d/c ≈ 1.5 > 1 with delay → unstable)
_provenance.posture: weak compliant posture only on axes with no task and no gravitational role: hip / knee axial rotation and the arms; spine axial rotations EXCLUDED (D12: their delayed posture loop drove a slow lateral spine oscillation); kRelax 0.85 × entry short-range stiffness, ζ 0.2 (S2)
_provenance.noise: motor noise (force level, seeded, low-pass 0.1 s), cv 0.025 of the entry tonic force per axis [D] (PPR-3)
_provenance.predict: variant B only: internal model of the ML COM mode over each channel’s delay from delayed observations + efference copy (no disturbance knowledge); Gg = measured mode stiffness, Ki = measured low-frequency intrinsic share (0.279 AP, 0.115 ML) [E]; muscle = canonical MUSCLE_GROUPS ankle.plantarflexion (AP) and hip.abduction (ML); axes [AP false, ML true] (D7: AP prediction degraded AP on the full body); source: AP from the ankle channel, ML from the hip channel

b2.apI.band: 10.6 mm = 2.58 × 4.1 mm: the ±99 % range of human quiet-stance COM AP excursion (COM RMS AP 4.1–4.3 mm, Foulger 2025, PPR-3 / BALANCE-1 U4 source; lower end) [M→E]. The AP COM integral (BALANCE-1 kI 0.17 s⁻¹, unchanged) integrates only inside it and holds outside (anti-windup; BALANCE2_AUDIT.md §6 phases 4–7)
b2.support: functional support of the entry stance from the entry COM (B2_GEOMETRY.json, measured): front 64.8 mm = mean of COM→MTP1 79.8 and COM→MTP5 49.9 (the oblique flat-foot pivot line; the measured COP plateau in §6 is ≈ 65 mm); back 124.76 mm = COM→heel edge. Check [M]: the implied maximum ankle moment m·g·(60.5 + 64.8) mm = 90.9 N·m vs Kim et al. 2009 maximum allowable flat-foot ankle torque 0.073 × BW × H = 93.2 ± 12.8 N·m
b2.effSupport: the internal model's developed AP force is bounded by what the support transmits at the propagated offset (COP shift (F + Ki·x)/(M·g/h) within [−back, +front]); the command itself is NOT capped
b2.dirMuscle: canonical MUSCLE_GROUPS: ankle.plantarflexion τ rise 146.7 / fall 54.2 ms (B's existing AP constants) for plantarflexion-direction force; ankle.dorsiflexion τ rise 88.8 / fall 95.3 ms for dorsiflexion-direction force (selected by the sign of the modelled activation)
b2.predict.axes: [AP true, ML true]: the AP mode now uses B's internal model (efference copy + measured Gg / Ki, re-anchored on each delayed observation); D7's 'AP worse' was the uncalibrated gain-1 model
b2.unchanged: every other parameter is BALANCE-1 B (B1_B.json): delays, channels, gains, groups, knee, support symmetry, posture, ML prediction, noise

c3.governor: mode force selected on DEV by the rule declared in C3_DESIGN_LOG.md D0 (before any C3 development run): eligible = no boot-tip load in any DEV non-fall case / bisection level / quiet standing; highest DEV forward 100 ms threshold (force 12.42 vs command 11.48, activation 11.48; C2 16.64 not eligible: tip share 1.00 at every non-fall level ≥ 15 N·s). Envelope = C2 b2.support unchanged (B2_GEOMETRY.json; Kim 2009). horizonSteps 120 (0.5 s > 3 × the slowest modelled time constant 146.7 ms), iters 20, tolN 0.01: numerical constants, not tuned
c3.unchanged: every other parameter is C2 (successor/params/C2.json), itself BALANCE-1 B except the three C2 mechanisms

b3.coordinate: mean sagittal hip angle = the H eigenmovement of a rigid-trunk model (Alexandrov 2005: ‘forward trunk bending, upper and lower body moving in opposite directions’); no overlap with the lumbar / thoracic or COM objectives (BALANCE3_BODY_AUDIT.md §4)
b3.KS: 1.15 = Alexandrov 2005 Table 1 H-mode K_S (mean, ± 0.07), × G_H (trunk gravitational stiffness about the hips, entry statics, 145.9 N·m/rad); applied as the controller term on top of M1b intrinsic stiffness — the same convention BALANCE-1 uses for the COM (Peterka) and knee objectives
b3.KV: 0.17 s = Alexandrov 2005 Table 1 H-mode K_V (mean, ± 0.02), × G_H
b3.delays: angle on hipAng = 18 steps = 75 ms (≥ Alexandrov H-mode effective delay 66.1 ± 10.2 ms, rounded up to BALANCE-1’s hip/trunk latency); rate on the existing orientRate (8 steps = 30 ms, proprioceptive velocity, Goodworth & Peterka 2009)
b3.integral: none (no fitted human eigenmovement / per-mode model includes integral action; research §10c)
b3.ankleCompanion: 0.141 = the ankle torque per unit hip torque that cancels the hip torque’s COM shift on THIS body: open-loop replay at 400 ms (hip 5 N·m → COM −0.364 mm; ankle 5 N·m → +2.588 mm; B3_IDENTIFY_OPENLOOP.json), the timescale nearest the H-mode time constant 0.48 s (Alexandrov [E]); Alexandrov 2001: the ankle eigenmovement compensates trunk-induced COM shift
b3.flexSign: +1: a forward trunk rotation about the hips increases the anatomical hip angle (P8 diagnosis: pelvis +1.2° with hip +1.0°); verified by the pre-freeze construction check
b3.unchanged: every C3 parameter and mechanism; BALANCE-1’s HAT AP objective stays as it is (its AP map ≈ 0; ML unchanged)
